properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Always obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,
always have a floatation device with you and swim near a
lifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel
to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 25 at 4:57AM CDT until September 25 at 11:00AM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande at Rio Grande near Castolon, Texas affecting Brewster
County.

For the Rio Grande...including Rio Grande near Castolon,  Texas...
Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Rio Grande near Castolon, Texas.

* WHEN...Until this morning.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, the river reaches bankfull, and no
significant damage is expected. At 15.0 feet, the river reaches
minor flood stage, and lowland flooding begins.  The river begins
to flood the road between Santa Elena Canyon and Cottonwood
Campground in Big Bend National Park.  The river begins to flood
the parking lot at Santa Elena Canyon, and cut off the nature trail
into the canyon.  Campers in Cottonwood Campground need to prepare
for possible evacuations. At 19.0 feet, the river reaches moderate
flood stage, and begins flooding Cottonwood Campground.  The river
inundates the restrooms upstream at Santa Elena Canyon parking lot.
The river begins to close all area roads.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:15 AM CDT Friday the stage was 17.7 feet (5.4 meters).
- Bankfull stage is 13.0 feet (4.0 meters).
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:15 AM CDT Friday was 17.8 feet (5.4 meters).
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage this
morning and continue falling to 2.7 feet (0.8 meters) early
Wednesday morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet (4.6 meters).
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.7
feet (5.4 meters) on 09/03/2024.

properties.description:

southern Sacramento Mountains with rainfall rates of 0.50 to 1 inch
per hour over a broad, saturated area in complex terrain.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and rain gauge indicated.

areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Canyon and Hay Canyon.

Tularosa Basin. Rainfall rates of up to 1 inch per hour have been
observed in heavier downpours north of Timberon and near Mayhill.

Rio Penasco, Agua Chiquita Creek, Bluewater Creek, Dry Burnt
Canyon, Elk Canyon, Lower Portions of Hay Canyon, Cox Canyon, and
James Canyon.


The most serious flooding impacts will be in downstream locations
including Mayhill, Sacramento, and Weed.

There are some signs that precipitation will begin to diminish
between 4 AM and 5 AM, but runoff will continue for some time
afterwards.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued September 24 at 11:47AM AKDT until September 26 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels on average of 1.5 to 2.5 feet above the
normal highest tide line. Southeast winds 40 to 50 mph with
gusts up to 70 mph expected. South winds 30 to 40 mph with
gusts to 50 mph expected Friday.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast including Kwigillingok and
Kipnuk.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will be multiple peaks in water
levels for the Kuskokwim Delta this morning through Saturday
morning coinciding with high tide cycles and strong southerly
winds. Southeast winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts to 60 mph this
afternoon will diminish early Friday until the low pressure
system moves west of the coast by Friday afternoon. Then, winds
will become southerly at 30 to 40 mph with gusts to 50 mph by
Friday afternoon. Winds gradually weaken but remain southerly
through Saturday.

For Kwigillingok, water levels reach 1.5 to 2.5 feet above the
normal highest tide line today, coinciding with the passage of a
frontal system. Water levels could reach up to 5 feet in a worst
case scenario. If water levels rise to 2.5 feet, impacts would be
comparable to the August 2024 storm.

For Kipnuk, the highest water levels of 1.5 to 2.5 feet above the
normal highest tide line are expected on Friday as a low pressure
system moves west of the coast and winds become southerly. Water
levels could reach 2 to 3 feet in a worst case scenario.

For more information regarding potential local flood impacts,
please reference maps.dggs.alaska.gov/akfit/
